title: test-0119-SCI-ESS-POLLUTION
passage: Many people believe that if water looks crystal clear and has no smell, it is perfectly safe to drink. However, this is a dangerous misconception. Water can contain invisible chemical pollutants like pesticides, lead, or arsenic that do not change the appearance of the liquid. Simply boiling water is a common household practice, but it only kills harmful germs; it does not remove dissolved chemical toxins. Similarly, some think that adding chlorine tablets is a magical solution that cleans all types of pollution. In reality, while chlorine is excellent for disinfecting water by killing bacteria, it cannot filter out heavy metals or industrial chemicals. Another common error is the belief that air pollution is only present when we see thick smoke or smell something foul. In truth, many dangerous gases are colourless and odourless. Furthermore, the greenhouse effect is not inherently a human-made disaster. It is a natural process that keeps our planet warm enough to support life. The problem arises when human activities increase greenhouse gases, trapping too much heat and causing global warming. We must look beyond what our eyes can see to understand the true state of our environment and protect our health from hidden threats.
